title: Task-Adaptive Few-shot Node Classification

problem.claim: Few-shot node classification must handle real-world graphs in which many classes have only limited labeled nodes.

gap.claim: GNN performance decreases substantially in few-shot node classification because task variance creates a large generalization gap between meta-training and meta-test tasks.

contributions.claim: A task-adaptive node classification framework is proposed for few-shot learning.
The framework accumulates meta-knowledge from classes with abundant labeled nodes and transfers it to classes with limited labeled nodes through task-adaptive modules.
Three modules perform node-level, class-level, and task-level adaptations within each meta-task to accommodate differing node and class distributions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The framework is reported to improve model generalization performance on meta-test tasks.
Extensive experiments on four node classification datasets are reported to demonstrate superiority over state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report that code is provided in a GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Node classification is important, while real-world graphs commonly contain many classes with few labeled nodes.
GNN performance drops in few-shot settings because node-level and class-level task variance causes a generalization gap between meta-training and meta-test tasks.
The proposed framework accumulates meta-knowledge from well-labeled classes and transfers it to sparsely labeled classes using task-adaptive modules.
Node-level, class-level, and task-level adaptations are applied within each meta-task to accommodate distribution differences.
Experiments on four node classification datasets are reported to outperform state-of-the-art baselines, and code is reported as available.

source_observation.claim: Task variance from differing node and class distributions is identified as a cause of the meta-training to meta-test generalization gap.

interpretation.claim: Few-shot transfer may benefit from adapting to the structure of each task instead of relying only on globally shared representations.

application.claim: For related few-shot graph problems, consider separate adaptations for node-level, class-level, and task-level distribution differences.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these adaptations help outside the reported node classification setting or under different task distributions.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the four datasets or report quantitative results.
The architecture and implementation details of the three adaptation modules are unspecified.
The few-shot protocol, meta-task construction, and baseline configurations are unspecified.
